summary: Long Island's 1897 iron light tower at Chequamegon Bay, Ashland County: a Coast Guard light until 1986, now being dismantled by the National Park Service in 2026.

light.characteristic_note: Red until 1947, green after (LighthouseFriends); the Park Service describes the historic aids as replaced by an offshore buoy.

structures.note: Moved about 100 feet in 1987; being dismantled in 2026.

access.note: Reached by water; Long Island is hard to reach (National Park Service). Grounds open and tower closed (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: National Park Service (Apostle Islands National Lakeshore)

events.note: Act of 1 October 1888 authorized a fog signal for the east-side light at Chequamegon Bay (Board report; LighthouseFriends gives 2 March 1889)
Act authorized removing and rebuilding the main light and a harbor light and bell at Chequamegon Point, not to exceed $10,000
Act approved 2 March 1895 provided $10,000 to move and rebuild the La Pointe light and establish a harbor bell and light at Chequamegon Point
Light established 11 October 1897: fixed red light and fog bell in operation
Three log cribs placed on the point to protect it from erosion
Lights at the point and La Pointe electrified
Characteristic changed from red to green
Discontinued (USLHS); Long Island added to Apostle Islands National Lakeshore the same year
Tower moved about 100 feet (NPS: east) because of shoreline change; a new light set up on a D9 cylindrical tower (LighthouseFriends)
Bent legs straightened and tower set on new concrete footings (2006-2008)
NPS announced dismantling (May 2026); contract awarded in August; work expected to conclude by 31 October 2026

corrections.why: The Park Service (May 2026) says the historic aids on Long Island have been replaced by a single Coast Guard buoy offshore and that the tower is being removed. USLHS gives 'Year Discontinued: 1986'.
USLHS gives 42 ft for the height of the light above mean high water, and the Park Service calls the tower 42 feet. 11.0 m does not match either.
USLHS gives the light at 42 ft (12.8 m) above mean high water. The 10.1 m figure is not supported by a checked source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikidata gives 1987 as the first lighting; the Board's report and the USLHS record give 11 October 1897. The 1987 date is the move of the tower and a new light on a D9 tower (LighthouseFriends; Park Service), not the first lighting of the iron tower.
USLHS gives 1896 as the year the tower was established; LighthouseFriends says work on the tower began in summer 1896 and the light was established 11 October 1897. Both are stated.
OSM and Wikidata say active; USLHS says discontinued 1986; the Park Service (2026) says the historic aids have been replaced by an offshore buoy. Treated as discontinued.
Wikidata 13.0 m, OSM 33 m, USLHS 42 ft (12.8 m). The 42 ft figure is used; the OSM figure is not supported.
The Park Service says the 1987 move was 100 feet east; LighthouseFriends says about 100 feet inland. The story gives the distance only.
The Board's 1892 report says the act of 1 October 1888 authorized the fog signal; LighthouseFriends gives an appropriation on 2 March 1889. The story uses the Board's date.

The sentence on the act of 1 October 1888 is in the report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1892 (scan p.547). Scan p.204 is in the report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1891 and is not cited for the 1892 sentence.

notes_for_editor: Open items: The 1896 Board report prints 'finished ou March 18,1890' (OCR); the story uses LighthouseFriends's 'March 18, 1896' and the Board's 1896 volume year. The 1897 Board note reads 'The light wns established October 11, 1897' (OCR); the story gives the date without quoting the OCR. The 1987 move direction disagrees: NPS says 100 feet east; LighthouseFriends says about 100 feet inland. Both are stated in the story. The NPS August 2026 release gives a $135,000 contract. A Friends of the Apostle Islands repost and a Govly listing give $167,400. The story does not give a figure. Work was due to finish by 31 October 2026; no report after the August 2026 release was read, so the story does not say the removal is complete. The current characteristic is not verified: LighthouseFriends gives green from 1947, the record gives Fl G 4s from ENC, and the Park Service calls the aid decommissioned. No keepers are named for the point in the USLHS record; LighthouseFriends says the La Pointe keepers maintained it. The keepers array is empty. The 'Storms, wrecks and rescues' chapter is omitted: no storm, wreck or rescue tied to the point was found in the sources read. Wikipedia was consulted for leads only and is not cited. The 1858 La Pointe light and its move are the La Pointe station's history and appear here only as context.
